detail: The prod profile uses sslmode require; the server's certificate is not verified.
remedy: Set sslmode to verify-full (or verify-ca) in the profile and give the server's CA.

detail: The prod profile sets no sslmode; the server's certificate is not verified.
remedy: Set sslmode to verify-full (or verify-ca) in the profile and give the server's CA.

detail: The profile uses sslmode prefer for a host that is not loopback: traffic can be read or changed on the way (T-10).
remedy: Use sslmode verify-full.

detail: The profile says read_only_role, but the role, or a role it can SET ROLE to, may write in 1 table, view or sequence (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, a column grant or ownership). Studio's session is read-only; the role is not.
remedy: Connect with a role that has only SELECT (and USAGE on the schemas), no CREATE on any schema, no TEMP on the database, and no membership in a role that can write.

detail: The profile says read_only_role, but the role, or a role it can SET ROLE to, may write in 3 tables, views or sequences (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, a column grant or ownership); and create tables in 1000+ schemas (CREATE on the schema); and create temporary tables (TEMP on the database). Studio's session is read-only; the role is not.
remedy: Connect with a role that has only SELECT (and USAGE on the schemas), no CREATE on any schema, no TEMP on the database, and no membership in a role that can write.

detail: The profile says read_only_role, but the role, or a role it can SET ROLE to, may create tables in 1 schema (CREATE on the schema). Studio's session is read-only; the role is not.
remedy: Connect with a role that has only SELECT (and USAGE on the schemas), no CREATE on any schema, no TEMP on the database, and no membership in a role that can write.

detail: The profile says read_only_role, but the role, or a role it can SET ROLE to, may create temporary tables (TEMP on the database; PostgreSQL grants it to PUBLIC by default). Studio refuses the statements that create them and drops temporary tables when a session goes back to its pool; the role itself is not limited.
remedy: REVOKE TEMP ON DATABASE ... FROM PUBLIC (and from the role), and GRANT it to the roles that need it.

detail: Neither the role nor the database sets statement_timeout (or the most specific setting is 0), so an application that sets none runs statements without a limit (unless postgresql.conf sets one, which this role cannot read).
remedy: ALTER ROLE ... SET statement_timeout = '30s' (or ALTER DATABASE), or set it in the application (tabrion's SessionSettings does).

detail: PRAGMA foreign_key_check finds 1 row whose foreign key points nowhere: data was written with foreign_keys off.
remedy: Open the database with foreign_keys on (tabrion.sqlite.connect does) and repair the rows.

detail: PRAGMA foreign_key_check finds 1000+ rows whose foreign key points nowhere: data was written with foreign_keys off.
remedy: Open the database with foreign_keys on (tabrion.sqlite.connect does) and repair the rows.

detail: The role owns, or can become the owner of, 1 table or view in the database; an owner can change it and is not subject to row-level security unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set.
remedy: Use an owner role for migrations and a separate runtime role for the application.

detail: The role owns, or can become the owner of, 42 tables or views in the database; an owner can change them and is not subject to row-level security unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set.
remedy: Use an owner role for migrations and a separate runtime role for the application (03 section 5.4: required for prod).

detail: Default privileges (ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES) grant the role, or a role it belongs to, write access to tables or sequences created later.
remedy: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE ON TABLES FROM the role.

detail: The diagnosis stopped because you canceled it. Not run: tabrion's checks, STU-DX-003, backup hints.
remedy: Run the diagnosis again; for a large SQLite file, give the profile a longer statement timeout.

detail: The diagnosis stopped because it reached the time limit of 15 s. Not run: tabrion's integrity check (TAB-SQ-006), STU-DX-005.
remedy: Run the diagnosis again; for a large SQLite file, give the profile a longer statement timeout.

detail: The diagnosis stopped because it reached the time limit of 0.5 s. Not run: backup hints.
remedy: Run the diagnosis again; for a large SQLite file, give the profile a longer statement timeout.

detail: PRAGMA foreign_key_check failed: a foreign key definition is broken, for example it points at columns without a primary key or unique index.
remedy: Fix the foreign key definitions (the parent columns need a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint).

detail: PRAGMA foreign_key_check could not run: the database was busy, locked or not readable.
remedy: Run the diagnosis again when no other program holds a lock on the file.

detail: Neither the role nor the database sets lock_timeout; an application that sets none runs without them (unless postgresql.conf sets them, which this role cannot read).
remedy: ALTER ROLE ... SET (or ALTER DATABASE), or set them in the application (tabrion's SessionSettings does).

detail: Neither the role nor the database sets lock_timeout, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, application_name; an application that sets none runs without them (unless postgresql.conf sets them, which this role cannot read).
remedy: ALTER ROLE ... SET (or ALTER DATABASE), or set them in the application (tabrion's SessionSettings does).

detail: Studio found no SQLite file next to the database, or in its backups or backup subfolder, whose name starts with the database's name. Backups kept elsewhere are not visible to Studio.
remedy: Back the database up with tabrion.sqlite.backup (online, 0600, checked with quick_check) and keep the copy on another disk as well.

detail: The newest backup is 1 minute older than the database's last change.
remedy: Make a new backup with tabrion.sqlite.backup, for example before every migration.

detail: The newest backup is 90 minutes older than the database's last change.
remedy: Make a new backup with tabrion.sqlite.backup, for example before every migration.

detail: The newest backup is 1 hour older than the database's last change.
remedy: Make a new backup with tabrion.sqlite.backup, for example before every migration.

detail: The newest backup is 2 hours older than the database's last change.
remedy: Make a new backup with tabrion.sqlite.backup, for example before every migration.

detail: The newest backup is 1 day older than the database's last change.
remedy: Make a new backup with tabrion.sqlite.backup, for example before every migration.

detail: The newest backup is 8 days older than the database's last change.
remedy: Make a new backup with tabrion.sqlite.backup, for example before every migration.

detail: 1 backup file can be read by the group or by others; a backup holds all the data.
remedy: chmod 600 the backup files; tabrion.sqlite.backup creates them with 0600.

detail: 3 backup files can be read by the group or by others; a backup holds all the data.
remedy: chmod 600 the backup files; tabrion.sqlite.backup creates them with 0600.

detail: Studio could not list the database's folder or one of its backup subfolders.
remedy: Check the folder's permissions, or look for backups yourself.

detail: A folder holds more than 10000 entries; Studio looked at the first 10000 of each (in no particular order), so a backup, even the newest one, may not have been seen.
remedy: Keep backups in a backups subfolder of their own, or fewer files next to the database.

detail: archive_mode is off: the server keeps no WAL archive, so the database cannot be restored to a point in time. Studio cannot see backups made with pg_dump or with a tool that does not archive WAL.
remedy: Make sure the database is backed up (pg_dump, pg_basebackup or a backup tool); for point-in-time recovery set archive_mode and an archive_command or archive_library.

detail: The archiver failed 1 time since its statistics were reset, and the last attempt failed: the WAL archive has a gap and the server keeps WAL until archiving works again.
remedy: Look at the server log for the archive_command or archive_library error and fix it.

detail: The archiver failed 7 times since its statistics were reset, and the last attempt failed: the WAL archive has a gap and the server keeps WAL until archiving works again.
remedy: Look at the server log for the archive_command or archive_library error and fix it.

detail: archive_mode is on, but the archiver has not archived a WAL file since its statistics were reset.
remedy: Check that archive_command or archive_library is set; pg_switch_wal() forces a first file.

detail: The server is a standby with archive_mode on, which archives only on the primary.
remedy: Check the archiving on the primary, or set archive_mode = always to archive on the standby too.

detail: Studio could not read archive_mode or pg_stat_archiver with this role.
remedy: Ask the database administrator how the database is backed up.
